uncertainty-resolves-toward-the-candidat.statement: Where the system is unsure and the outcome is adverse, it must fail closed — toward the person, away from the automated action. An unclassifiable candidate is shielded from automated rejection rather than defaulted into an unprotected class. A malformed or unrecognised verdict becomes *hold*, never *advance* and never *reject*. A tie at an irreversible cutoff spares the whole tied group rather than splitting it by arrival order. An unknown education level skips a gate instead of failing it.

no-adverse-outcome-is-solely-automated.statement: A machine may rank, sort, surface and recommend. A person makes every advance, offer and rejection. Rejection is never a routable automated outcome: a model may *recommend* reject, but the machine-actionable route admits only advance or hold, and anything else parks at a human gate.

meaning-does-not-live-in-a-label.statement: Teams rename their stages, split their columns, invent their own titles and grade people on their own scales. Nothing may derive meaning from a display string. Rules key off a stable role vocabulary — entry, screening, interview, offer, terminal — so a renamed board does not silently change what the fairness metric measures or tell an offer-stage candidate that their résumé has been received.

a-claim-carries-its-sample-and-its-basis.statement: Every rate, ratio, band and verdict states what it was computed over and how many observations stand behind it, and refuses to render when that number is too small to support it. A conversion rate needs a real stage transition, not an inferred one. A selection-rate ratio needs a cohort large enough for a proportion to be stable. A comparative claim needs at least two things to compare. A peer benchmark needs enough contributors that no contributor is identifiable.

absence-of-evidence-is-not-evidence.statement: An unrecorded claim, an unscored candidate, an unmeasured metric, a check that did not run, a competency the conversation never reached — none of these may render as a value, a zero, a neutral constant, or a pass. Each needs a distinct state that says *not measured*.

a-verdict-is-bound-to-what-it-judged.statement: A quality verdict binds to the exact content and the exact rubric that produced it. Re-produced content inherits neither the pass nor the condemnation. A verdict scored under a superseded rubric is marked superseded rather than silently re-meant, and a rating stamps the version of the scale it was scored on so a later revision cannot retroactively mark an axis off-rubric.

say-only-what-the-record-holds.statement: A rejection reason, a feedback line, a rationale, an advertisement, a market figure: each says what was actually recorded, in the words the record holds, or says nothing. Never invent a gap the candidate's own evidence disproves. Never advise adding something their profile already shows. Never imply a conversation that did not happen. Never fabricate a testimonial, a benefit, or a salary the role never stated.

a-predictor-cannot-grade-its-own-labels.statement: When a score causes an outcome, that outcome cannot validate the score. A screening threshold that rejects below a floor produces the very rejections a reliability curve would score it against, so a perfectly biased screener draws a perfect diagram. The coupling must be named wherever the curve is shown, and broken by a clean arm — a stable, deterministic holdout of candidates the score would have acted on but did not.

inference-must-look-like-inference.statement: A model's guess must never render in the visual or linguistic grammar reserved for measurement. A self-reported confidence is evidence about the model, not about the person, and does not get the tone band a measured quantity gets. An enrichment is labelled as an enrichment; a heuristic reading of a career is a hypothesis carrying a suggested probe, not a verdict. A document yields hypotheses; a conversation yields evidence; only a demonstration yields proof, and the three are never shown alike.

a-candidates-process-never-stalls-on-you.statement: Your outage, your quota, your rate limit and your billing state are yours. A candidate's own action — accepting an offer, booking a slot, submitting an application, asking for their data — must not fail because of them. Metered work a recruiter initiates may be blocked honestly; a candidate's action is debited and never gated.

every-decision-names-its-actor.statement: A decision about a person records who or what made it: a named human, or the automated process, with a third honest state for "cannot determine". A null actor renders as *not identified*, never as a default person. A human reversing a machine's decision seals to the reverser and never inherits the machine's attribution. Authority may be downgraded from human to automated when the record is unclear, never upgraded.
